en: Conditioned by this internal [contact], there arises a pleasant feeling to be experienced.
A certain monk [recited] three sūtras. The Venerable Ānanda [recited] three... [The internal sense-sphere (ādhyātmikam āyatanam) was taught by the Blessed One but not yet analyzed...
...the mind (manas) is the internal sense-sphere, and that was [taught] by the Blessed One...
Formless, invisible, and non-obstructive... [the sphere]... four spheres... verso eno89_2... [the sphere]... four spheres...
"Just as sound is with resistance (*sapratigha*), so too...
"Venerable sir, external bases (*bāhyam āyatana*) are said to be with resistance.
And the monk asked Brahmā: "Does everything exist? And what are all phenomena (*sarvadharma*)?"
What are the six external sense bases? Which six? Form is the external [sense base]. Catalogue No. 1879, recto.
And the brahmin Ānanda, the monk, asks about the dharmas: "The Teacher, the monk...

the eye is an internal sense-sphere (*ādhyātmikam āyatanaṃ*); the ear, nose, tongue, body... sound, taste, tangible objects, and mental phenomena (*dharma*) are external sense-spheres (*bāhyam āyatanaṃ*). There are six consciousnesses..."
...these six: eye-contact, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind-contact.
Feeling born of contact. These six are the groups of perception (*saṃjñākāya*); which six? Eye-... [verso]

Volition born of contact with the eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; [volition] regarding forms, sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and phenomena. These six are the fallow ground of the mind and the stains. These phenomena are with outflows and subject to grasping; they are the basis for the fallow ground of the mind and the stains.
"Monks, the eye—whether past or future—is impermanent. Who would delight in it?
For the sake of revulsion toward the present eye, for dispassion, and for its cessation..."
